title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
shortDescription: Oxygen sensor heater control circuit reads high voltage for Bank 1 Sensor 3.
fullDescription:
P0044 sets when the PCM sees the heater control circuit for the third oxygen sensor on Bank 1 stuck high (open driver or short to B+). Bank 1 Sensor 3 is typically a downstream sensor in vehicles with multiple post-catalyst sensors.

Until the sensor reaches operating temperature, fueling decisions for that bank may be biased and the catalyst monitor will not run.
safetyImpact: None directly; fuel economy and emissions affected.

causes.cause: Open heater element in O2 sensor
Wiring open between PCM and sensor

fixSteps.title: Probe heater control wire
fixSteps.instruction: Backprobe the heater control wire at the sensor; should pulse to ground with key on.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If the heater is open and wiring is good, replace the O2 sensor.

faq.a: No; required for catalyst efficiency monitor.

title: HO2S Heater Resistance (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
shortDescription: Bank 1 Sensor 3 oxygen sensor heater resistance out of range.
fullDescription: P0049 indicates the calculated heater resistance for Bank 1 Sensor 3 is outside the expected window (typically 2-15 ohms cold, ramping with temperature). Aging sensors and harness corrosion are common causes.

fixSteps.title: Measure heater resistance cold
fixSteps.instruction: Compare to spec at room temperature.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace if outside spec.

faq.a: Stick with OEM-style for accurate heater curve.

title: HO2S Heater Resistance (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
shortDescription: Heater resistance out of spec for Bank 1 Sensor 3.
fullDescription: P0055 is the resistance-based variant for Bank 1 Sensor 3 heater. The PCM applies a brief pulse and infers heater health from current draw. Aged elements draw too little; shorted ones too much.

fixSteps.title: Measure cold resistance
fixSteps.instruction: DMM across heater pins per OEM spec.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace if not within spec.

faq.a: Most modern sensors come pre-coated; do not add more to the tip.

title: Turbocharger Boost Control Circuit Performance (Variant)
shortDescription: Wastegate or VGT actuator response not tracking command.
fullDescription:
P0046 (variant) sets when commanded vs actual boost solenoid duty cycle or VGT vane position fall outside the expected dynamic envelope. Common on diesel VGT systems where soot fouls vanes.

This collision suffix variant covers cases where the OEM uses the same code differently from generic P0046 already in the catalog.

fixSteps.title: Actuator self-test
fixSteps.instruction: Use scan tool to cycle VGT actuator full sweep.

fixSteps.title: Clean or replace VGT
fixSteps.instruction: Soot soak or replace if vanes are stuck.

faq.a: Sustained highway driving may free mild soot accumulation.

title: Turbocharger Boost Control Solenoid Circuit Low (Variant)
shortDescription: Boost control solenoid driver reads low.
fullDescription: P0047 (variant) sets when the boost control solenoid driver circuit reads ground when it should be off, indicating a short to ground or stuck-on driver. The PCM disables boost as a safety measure.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: If P0047 changes to P0048, solenoid is shorted.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Look for chafing against turbo or exhaust.

fixSteps.title: Replace solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Replace if coil resistance out of spec.

faq.a: Not recommended; engine performance and fueling depend on it.

title: Fuel Timing Error
shortDescription: Diesel fuel injection timing deviates from commanded.
fullDescription:
P0149 is set when the PCM compares commanded fuel injection timing to crank/cam-derived actual timing and finds the spread outside specification. On older diesels with a cam-driven pump, this often points to a worn timing advance mechanism. On common-rail systems, it can indicate injector synchronization issues.

Driveability is degraded; emissions rise sharply.
safetyImpact: Reduced power; high emissions; possible limp mode.

causes.cause: Crank or cam sensor signal noise

fixSteps.title: Verify crank/cam sync
fixSteps.instruction: Scope crank and cam signals; check correlation.

fixSteps.title: Inspect injection pump
fixSteps.instruction: Check timing advance per OEM procedure.

fixSteps.title: Service or replace pump
fixSteps.instruction: Refurbish or replace as required.

faq.a: Cetane improver may mask but not fix mechanical timing issues.

title: Cylinder 9 Injector Circuit (Variant)
shortDescription: Injector circuit fault on cylinder 9.
fullDescription:
P0209 (variant) sets on V10/V12 engines when the cylinder 9 injector driver detects an open or shorted load. Cause is typically a failed injector coil or harness damage from heat near the exhaust manifold.

This variant covers OEM-specific implementations where misfire and contribution thresholds differ from the catalog primary entry.
safetyImpact: Misfire; possible catalyst damage from raw fuel.

fixSteps.title: Swap injector
fixSteps.instruction: Move cyl 9 injector to a known good cylinder; see if code follows.

fixSteps.title: Replace if injector is at fault
fixSteps.instruction: Replace, prime fuel system.

faq.a: Often wise on high-mileage engines if one has failed.

title: Cylinder 11 Injector Circuit Low (Variant)
shortDescription: Cyl 11 injector driver reads low.
fullDescription: P0291 (variant) sets when the cylinder 11 injector driver sees a short to ground or stuck-on condition. PCM disables that injector to prevent damage. V12 engines and some industrial-derived powerplants are susceptible.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect injector
fixSteps.instruction: If code changes to P0292, injector is shorted.

fixSteps.title: Repair wiring or replace injector
fixSteps.instruction: As indicated.

faq.a: Yes for V12 with COP coils.

title: Cylinder 11 Injector Circuit High (Variant)
shortDescription: Cyl 11 injector driver reads high.
fullDescription: P0292 (variant) is set when the injector driver sees an open circuit or short to B+ on cylinder 11. Often points to a broken connector or harness pull-out near the valve cover.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Check for backed-out terminal.

fixSteps.title: Continuity test
fixSteps.instruction: Verify each leg from PCM to injector.

fixSteps.title: Replace as needed
fixSteps.instruction: Repair harness or swap injector.

faq.a: Diagnose injector and coil separately; symptoms overlap.

title: Cylinder 12 Injector Circuit (Variant)
shortDescription: Cyl 12 injector circuit fault.
fullDescription: P0293 (variant) covers a generic cyl 12 injector circuit fault that the OEM does not split into low/high variants. Commonly seen on V12 luxury engines.

fixSteps.title: Verify circuit
fixSteps.instruction: DMM continuity from PCM to injector.

fixSteps.title: Repair
fixSteps.instruction: Replace damaged component.

faq.a: PCM may disable cyl 12; expect rough idle.

title: Cylinder 12 Injector Circuit Low (Variant)
shortDescription: Cyl 12 injector driver reads low.
fullDescription: P0294 (variant) sets when the cyl 12 injector driver sees a short to ground or stuck-on. Commonly resolved by injector replacement after harness inspection.

fixSteps.title: Isolate
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect injector; if code changes to high, injector is shorted.

fixSteps.title: Repair
fixSteps.instruction: Wiring or injector.

faq.a: Unlikely if caught quickly; runaway fuel only with stuck-open injector.

title: Cylinder 12 Injector Circuit High
shortDescription: Cyl 12 injector driver reads high (open).
fullDescription: P0295 sets when the PCM reports an open circuit on the cylinder 12 injector driver. Most commonly an unplugged injector connector or broken harness wire.
safetyImpact: Cyl 12 inactive; raw air pumped through cylinder.

fixSteps.title: Connector check
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat and inspect for corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Coil resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Measure injector coil per spec.

fixSteps.title: Replace as required
fixSteps.instruction: Wiring or injector.

faq.a: Short distance OK; long drives risk catalyst damage.

title: Cylinder Range/Performance
shortDescription: One cylinder contribution outside expected range.
fullDescription: P0296 (range/performance) sets when relative cylinder contribution analysis (often crank-speed-based) shows one cylinder consistently producing less torque than its peers without specific misfire counts. Common cause is a mechanical issue (low compression, leaking valve) or a partially clogged injector.

causes.cause: Vacuum leak local to one runner

fixSteps.title: Cylinder contribution test
fixSteps.instruction: Use scan tool live data to identify weak cylinder.

fixSteps.title: Compression test
fixSteps.instruction: Verify mechanical integrity.

fixSteps.title: Address root cause
fixSteps.instruction: Clean injectors, rebuild head, or repair vacuum leak.

faq.a: Yes; P030x reacts to specific misfire counts. P0296 is contribution-based.

title: Vehicle Overspeed Condition
shortDescription: Vehicle exceeded a manufacturer-defined overspeed threshold.
fullDescription:
P0297 logs an overspeed event when the vehicle exceeds a programmed maximum speed (often 110-130 mph or limited by tire rating). Many fleet vehicles, light trucks with restricted tires, and EVs use this as a fleet-management or warranty-protection feature.

The code may auto-clear or remain in history depending on OEM.

causes.cause: VSS calibration error after tire change

fixSteps.title: Verify tire size
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm tires match calibration; recalibrate if changed.

fixSteps.title: Clear code
fixSteps.instruction: Clear if benign.

faq.a: Some commercial fleets pull this code; consumer use rarely matters.

title: Engine Oil Over Temperature Condition
shortDescription: Oil temperature exceeded threshold.
fullDescription:
P0298 sets when measured engine oil temperature exceeds the safe limit (typically 140-150 C / 285-300 F). Triggers include towing in hot weather, low oil level, restricted oil cooler, or failing thermostat.

Prolonged operation under this condition accelerates oil degradation and bearing wear.
safetyImpact: Risk of engine damage if ignored.

fixSteps.title: Check oil level and condition
fixSteps.instruction: Top off if low; replace if degraded.

fixSteps.title: Inspect oil cooler
fixSteps.instruction: Clean cooler fins and verify coolant flow.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermostat if stuck
fixSteps.instruction: Test oil thermostat operation.

faq.a: Higher-spec synthetic tolerates heat better but does not fix root cause.

title: Glow Plug B Circuit High (Variant)
shortDescription: Glow plug control circuit B reads high.
fullDescription: P0384 (variant) sets when the glow plug controller detects an open or high-side fault on the B-circuit (typically cylinders 4-6 on inline-6 diesels or one bank on V8 diesels). Cold-start performance and emissions during warm-up are degraded.
safetyImpact: Hard cold start; white smoke; possible NOx spike.

fixSteps.title: Resistance test each plug
fixSteps.instruction: Plugs typically 0.5-2 ohm; open is bad.

fixSteps.title: Replace bad plugs
fixSteps.instruction: Replace as a set per bank.

faq.a: Replace as a set; mismatched age causes uneven warm-up.

title: Glow Plug Module Communication (Variant)
shortDescription: Glow plug control module not communicating.
fullDescription: P0386 (variant) sets when the dedicated glow plug control module is unreachable on the LIN or local bus from the engine ECU. Often a 12V supply or ground fault to the module.

fixSteps.title: Check module power
fixSteps.instruction: 12V at module pin per OEM.

fixSteps.title: Bus continuity
fixSteps.instruction: Verify LIN line from ECU to module.

fixSteps.title: Replace module
fixSteps.instruction: If supply and bus OK.

faq.a: In warm weather usually fine; cold weather risks no-start.

title: Glow Plug Bus Voltage Low (Variant)
shortDescription: Glow plug bus voltage below threshold.
fullDescription: P0387 (variant) sets when the glow plug bus voltage drops below the threshold during heat cycle. Most often a weak battery, marginal alternator, or high resistance in the supply path.

fixSteps.title: Battery load test
fixSteps.instruction: Verify CCA meets spec.

fixSteps.title: Inspect supply
fixSteps.instruction: Voltage drop test on glow plug supply.

fixSteps.title: Repair as needed
fixSteps.instruction: Battery, cables, or fusible link.

faq.a: Many diesels have two; both must be healthy.

title: Glow Plug Bus Voltage High (Variant)
shortDescription: Glow plug bus voltage above threshold.
fullDescription: P0388 (variant) sets when measured glow plug bus voltage exceeds spec, indicating a stuck-on relay or shorted control circuit forcing voltage to the bus when it should be off.
symptoms: Glow plugs hot when not commanded

fixSteps.title: Disconnect relay control
fixSteps.instruction: If bus stays hot, relay is welded.

fixSteps.title: Replace relay
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the glow plug relay or controller.

faq.a: Yes; disconnect glow plug relay until repaired.

title: Glow Plug Bus Voltage Intermittent (Variant)
shortDescription: Glow plug bus voltage drops intermittently.
fullDescription: P0389 (variant) sets on intermittent dropouts of the glow plug bus voltage. Vibration-induced relay contact bounce or a marginal connector are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Wiggle test
fixSteps.instruction: Tap relay and connectors with engine cold.

fixSteps.title: Replace marginal parts
fixSteps.instruction: Relay, connector, or busbar.

faq.a: Glow plug system is mostly idle once warm.

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A Range/Performance (Variant)
shortDescription: VSS A signal does not match expected range under driving conditions.
fullDescription: P0501 (variant) sets when the speed reported by the primary VSS does not align with cross-checks (transmission output speed, ABS wheel speed, GPS-derived). Typical causes include reluctor ring damage, magnetic debris on the sensor, and harness intermittents.
safetyImpact: Speedometer error; cruise control/limiter may disable.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and check for metal debris.

fixSteps.title: Measure air gap
fixSteps.instruction: Per OEM spec.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor or reluctor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace damaged components.

faq.a: Often yes if shared signals.

title: VSS A Circuit Low Input (Variant)
shortDescription: VSS A signal stays at low or 0 mph reading.
fullDescription: P0502 (variant) sets when the primary VSS reports zero or near-zero speed while other inputs (engine load, transmission speed) indicate the vehicle is moving. Indicates open circuit, missing reluctor, or sensor failure.

fixSteps.title: Check sensor wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Continuity from sensor to PCM.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If wiring intact.

faq.a: Limp shift schedule; harsh feel possible.

title: VSS A Intermittent/Erratic/High (Variant)
shortDescription: VSS A signal intermittent or noisy.
fullDescription: P0503 (variant) sets on intermittent or excessively noisy VSS A signal. Causes include damaged reluctor, marginal sensor air gap, EMI from aftermarket equipment, or harness damage.

fixSteps.title: Scope the signal
fixSteps.instruction: Capture VSS waveform under driving.

fixSteps.title: Inspect reluctor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove sensor and visually check teeth.

fixSteps.title: Replace as needed
fixSteps.instruction: Sensor or wiring repair.

faq.a: Possibly, if reluctor is damaged by debris on chains.

title: Idle Air Control Malfunction (Variant)
shortDescription: Idle speed cannot be maintained at target.
fullDescription: P0505 (variant) sets when the PCM cannot hold idle near the target. On older cars with IAC valves this often means a stuck valve; on drive-by-wire this means throttle plate carbon buildup or a failing throttle body.

fixSteps.title: Clean throttle body
fixSteps.instruction: Use throttle body cleaner; perform relearn after.

fixSteps.title: Smoke test for vacuum leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Detect any leaks in intake system.

fixSteps.title: Replace IAC or throttle body
fixSteps.instruction: If cleaning does not resolve.

faq.a: Yes; most modern cars require idle/throttle relearn after cleaning.

title: ECM Power Relay Sense Circuit Low
shortDescription: Main relay sense feedback to ECM reads low.
fullDescription:
P0689 sets when the ECM cannot detect proper voltage on its main-relay output sense input even though the relay should be closed. Causes include welded relay open, blown main fuse, or sense wire fault.

Frequently appears alongside intermittent no-start conditions where the ECM loses power briefly and resets.

fixSteps.title: Swap main relay
fixSteps.instruction: Try a known-good identical relay.

fixSteps.title: Check fuses
fixSteps.instruction: Verify ECM main and battery fuses.

fixSteps.title: Trace sense wire
fixSteps.instruction: Continuity from ECM to relay output.

faq.a: Relay contacts pit and arc; warm operation makes it worse.

title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Control Circuit Low (Variant)
shortDescription: ECM main relay control wire reads low when off.
fullDescription: P0686 (variant) sets when the ECM observes its own relay control output stuck low (i.e., commanded off but pulled to ground externally). Typically a wiring short or stuck relay coil.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect relay
fixSteps.instruction: If P0686 changes to P0687, relay coil is shorted.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Look for chafing.

faq.a: Different side: control vs sense. Both can coexist.

title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Control Circuit High (Variant)
shortDescription: ECM main relay control wire reads high when commanded on.
fullDescription: P0687 (variant) sets when the ECM cannot pull its relay control low (open coil or open wire). Frequently a failed relay or open trace inside the ECM.

fixSteps.title: Check coil resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Measure relay coil per spec.

fixSteps.title: Continuity to ECM
fixSteps.instruction: Verify control wire integrity.

fixSteps.title: Replace relay or repair wire
fixSteps.instruction: ECM replacement is last resort.

faq.a: Rare; verify simpler causes first.

title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Open (Variant)
shortDescription: ECM cannot read its relay output state.
fullDescription: P0688 (variant) is set when the relay output sense input to the ECM is open. ECM can still command but cannot confirm relay closure, so it sets the code as a precaution.

fixSteps.title: Test sense wire
fixSteps.instruction: Continuity check.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connector
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect ECM connector for backed-out pins.

faq.a: Yes if intermittent; expect possible stalls.

title: Normal/Performance Switch Circuit Malfunction (Variant)
shortDescription: Transmission mode-select switch circuit fault.
fullDescription: P0790 (variant) sets when the TCM cannot read a valid signal from the Normal/Performance (or similar Eco/Sport) switch. Driver-selected shift maps will revert to default.

causes.cause: Wiring open between switch and TCM

fixSteps.title: Test switch
fixSteps.instruction: Continuity through positions.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: If contacts intermittent.

faq.a: No; default map is safe.

title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor No Signal (Variant)
shortDescription: TCM not seeing intermediate shaft speed sensor signal.
fullDescription:
P0793 (variant) sets when the TCM expects a signal from the intermediate shaft sensor (used for ratio monitoring on stepped automatics) but sees none. Common cause is a failed sensor or chipped reluctor.

Without this signal, the TCM cannot verify gear ratios and may default to limp.

fixSteps.title: Check sensor wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Continuity and resistance per spec.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: External sensors are simple; internal require pan drop.

fixSteps.title: Inspect reluctor
fixSteps.instruction: Last resort if wiring and sensor are good.

faq.a: Short distances OK; long limp driving causes wear.
